_what_this_is: The entry gate, answered BEFORE drafting. The threshold question is whether a well-informed non-expert would confidently believe something the primary sources do not support.

belief._note: What the reader already believes, stated as they would state it. If you cannot write this sentence, there is nothing to correct and no subject -- which is how the tobacco-analogy candidate died.
belief.statement: Removing CO2 from the air is needed to reach net zero, but only as a small add-on to deep emission cuts. Tree planting helps a bit. Machines that suck CO2 from the air are expensive, tiny in scale and unproven. Leaning on removal risks becoming an excuse to keep burning fossil fuels.
belief.how_we_know_they_believe_it: The coverage that settled it. Named outlets, quoted headlines. Not 'it is widely assumed'.

outlet_unverified.sentence: We could not verify where this belief is published.
refused: Corporate Europe Observatory (https://corporateeurope.org/en/DeadlyClimateGamble): the page has 14 of the belief's 27 key words (needs 17)
National Observer (https://www.nationalobserver.com/2024/09/24/opinion/carbon-removal-emissions-reduction-hand-hand): a wall (challenge (headers)): not worked around
Fossil Free California (https://fossilfreeca.org/net-zero-is-a-false-narrative-and-a-dangerous-trap/): the page has 13 of the belief's 27 key words (needs 17)
outlet_unverified.by: code: no proposed outlet verified (a model's proposals, checked by code)

what_the_sources_show.statement: The IPCC synthesis says with high confidence that deploying CDR to counterbalance hard-to-abate residual emissions is unavoidable alongside deep and rapid cuts, and that CDR can also lower net emissions in the near term and achieve net negative emissions; Minx et al. say scenario evidence suggests the need for large-scale NETs in 1.5°C scenarios, amid deep uncertainties.
what_the_sources_show.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code

direction._note: CORRECTS, CONFIRMS or NARROWS. This field exists so the contrarianism guard can count. A publication whose answer is always CORRECTS is performing scepticism rather than assessing evidence, and is not to be trusted.
direction.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code
direction.why: The sources support removal as a necessary complement to deep cuts and the risk that it becomes an excuse, but they describe large-scale rather than small deployment in 1.5°C pathways, and none of the passages addresses the current scale or proven status of air-capture machines.

reader_with_a_decision: A policymaker, corporate sustainability lead or climate-conscious investor deciding how much weight, money and target-setting credit to give carbon removal versus direct emission reductions. For example: whether to count removals toward a net-zero pledge, buy removal credits, or fund removal procurement and R&D.

public_record_check._note: NOT 'has anybody published this'. On any contested question, somebody has. The question is whether it has been carried WHERE THIS READER WOULD FIND IT. Run the counterexample hunter on the belief statement, not on the finding.
public_record_check.our_contribution: translation, extension, or correction of the prior art -- say which

kill_condition: The primary assessments and inventories say what the belief already says, with nothing materially different. That would mean all four of these hold: removal is treated as necessary only to balance hard-to-abate residual emissions and, later, to draw temperatures down; it cannot substitute for near-term cuts; current removal is overwhelmingly conventional (forests and land) while novel methods are negligible in volume; and the projected scale-up is large but uncertain. If so, there is no story.

kill_condition_tested.by: a model's reading (claude-opus-5-5, from held sources), the quotation verified verbatim by code
kill_condition_tested.note: Three of the four conditions are partly shown: CDR is for residual emissions and later net-negative, it supplements rather than replaces cuts, and scale-up is large with 'deep uncertainties'; but the IPCC adds a near-term net-reduction role, and no passage gives current removal volumes split between

scope._note: What the answer will and will not cover, written at step 1 BEFORE any source is opened, so scope cannot be fitted to the findings afterwards. An omission ruled OUT_OF_SCOPE, and a headline conclusion declared out of scope, must name the question's words or one of these entries (fix 2, docs/whu-fix2-omission-rulings-design.md section 2.4).
scope.covers: The role of deliberate carbon dioxide removal in reaching net-zero CO2 and greenhouse gas emissions. This means both conventional land-based methods (afforestation, reforestation, soil carbon) and novel methods (direct air capture with storage, bioenergy with carbon capture and storage, enhanced weathering, biochar, ocean-based approaches). It covers how much removal happens today, how much assessed pathways say is needed by mid-century and beyond, and how removal relates to, and cannot replace, emission cuts. It also covers the main constraints on scaling up: cost, land, energy, storage permanence and monitoring.

out.what: Carbon capture and storage at the point of emission on fossil fuel plants or industry
out.why: This reduces new emissions rather than removing CO2 already in the air. It is a different accounting category.

out.what: Solar radiation modification or other sunlight-reflecting geoengineering
out.why: It does not remove CO2. It raises separate risk and governance questions.

out.what: Whether specific companies' or countries' offset claims are credible
out.why: That is an audit of individual projects and markets, not the system-level role of removal.

out.what: The cost-effectiveness ranking of particular removal start-ups or technologies for investment
out.why: It needs commercial data and project-level analysis beyond the question of overall role.

out.what: Non-CO2 greenhouse gas removal, such as methane removal
out.why: The question is specifically about carbon dioxide.

evidence_standard._note: What kinds of evidence the answer will weigh, written at step 1 BEFORE any source is opened (post-study fix 3, docs/whu-fix3-evidence-standard.md). 'measured': outcomes measured in trials, cohorts, evaluations. 'assessed': expert assessments -- systematic-review conclusions, IPCC confidence-rated statements, guideline recommendations. When they differ, the page states both and drops neither.
evidence_standard.measured: Inventoried or monitored quantities: current annual removal volumes split by conventional land-based and novel methods; the number and capacity of operating and planned direct air capture and bioenergy-with-capture facilities; tonnes actually delivered against removal purchases; observed costs per tonne; measured storage and permanence data; the size of national residual emissions reported in long-term strategies.
evidence_standard.assessed: Judgements by expert assessment bodies that carry stated confidence or likelihood language. Examples include a panel's high-confidence statement that removal is unavoidable to reach net zero; its assessed ranges for cumulative removal in pathways that limit warming to 1.5°C or 2°C; its confidence ratings on the feasibility, sustainability and side effects of each method; and its evaluation of the risk that relying on future removal delays emission cuts.
